key_insight: DED-Agent autonomously builds and calibrates laser directed energy deposition thermal models, reducing reported error to 0.9–2.5% within three calibration rounds.
engineering_relevance: Faster thermal model development could help engineers explore process parameters that influence defects, microstructure and properties.
method: A supervisor coordinates intent, simulation and calibration agents through a shared structured specification.
Agents translate plain-language requests into validated specifications and build, run and check finite element thermal models.
A high-order proper generalized decomposition surrogate accelerates trust-region calibration of heat-source parameters against experimental data.
evidence_signal: Across five benchmark builds, executable models were generated without manual intervention; surrogate predictions differed from full finite element results by 0.08–1.55%, with calibration accelerated 5–13×.
watch_item: Validation covers five benchmark builds; broader reliability and direct microstructure prediction are not established by the abstract.
paper_title: DED-Agent: An agentic AI method for autonomous thermal simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition
